name: Adonijah
overview: Adonijah was a male biblical figure noted as a non-Levite leader, specifically mentioned in Nehemiah 10:14 and named on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10:16. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership role is distinct among those listed. His presence in the text highlights his recognized position within the community.
namesAndTitles: The name Adonijah means '[my] lord is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord God. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:16 and does not appear to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Adonijah as a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader covenantal lineage of Israel as noted in Nehemiah 10:16. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Adonijah's role as a non-Levite leader mentioned in a covenantal context underscores his part in the community's religious and social commitments. His inclusion on a sealed document signifies trust and responsibility among the leaders of Israel. Although not detailed here, his narrative elsewhere reflects the consequences of ambition against God's chosen order, reinforcing the biblical principle of submission to divinely appointed authority.
